history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 374 (id "bhootnath-temple-mandi") - same temple, same town. A 16th-century Shikhara-style stone Shiva temple in the heart of Mandi town. Built in 1527 CE by Raja Ajber (Ajbar/Ajmer) Sen: legend says a cow was found offering its milk to a stone in the woods, after which Shiva appeared in the Raja's dream and told him to dig beneath it; the Raja unearthed the shivalinga and enshrined it here. With this temple the Raja founded the new township of Mandi and shifted his capital from Bhiuli (sources agree the capital moved with the temple's founding). Bhootnath ("lord of ghosts/spirits") is venerated as the guardian of the town, and the Raja began the observance of the Shivaratri festival here - the temple is the centre of the week-long Mandi Shivaratri fair at which over 200 local deities gather. A ghritkambal shringar tradition (the lingam covered with butter shaped into forms of Shiva during Tararatri before Mahashivratri) is reported in a video description (verify).

name: Bhootnath Temple
town_description: Mandi is a town on the Beas River in central Himachal Pradesh, called the 'Varanasi of the Hills' or 'Choti Kashi' for its 81 old stone temples. It was founded in the 16th century by Raja Ajber Sen, who moved his capital here from Bhiuli, and its temples and ghats line the river. Today Mandi is the commercial and transit hub of the central hills, famous for the week-long Mandi Shivaratri fair when hundreds of deities converge on the town.

travel.road: ~1 km from Mandi bus station, in the heart of the town; easy walk
